newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan chip industry seen picking up in '97.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan chip industry seen picking up in '97.

text.p: Lehman Brothers, the global investment bank, said on Tuesday it expects to see a turnaround in Taiwan's semiconductor industry by the second half of 1997.

The assessment comes in spite of current negative market sentiment towards investing in the industry and a slump in prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) and static random access memory (SRAM) chips.
Lehman Brothers said in a statement that it recommends that long-term investors take advantage of the prevailing negative sentiment to build up a semiconductor portfolio.
"Such a portfolio should outperform the market on a one-to-two-year horizon," said Richard Wei, technology analyst at Lehman Brothers Asia.

"The Taiwanese semiconductor industry is currently trading at a deep discount to the market," he said. "However, investors need to be selective. We prefer semiconductor service companies which mainly engage in the fabrication, packaging and testing of chips."

Wei acknowledged that the near-term outlook for the memory markets, especially DRAMs and SRAMs, "looks pessimistic." But he said the longer-term outlook for the industry remains attractive as the semiconductor content in electronics continues to rise and takes on more functionality.
"The current slow-down in unit growth should last only two to three more quarters. Overall unit demand will pick up in 1997-1998 due to the drastic price decline," Wei said.
The slowdown is also forcing semiconductor firms to reconsider or even postpone their capacity expansion plans, he said.
"This is a positive as the excess capacity could lead to further price slump," Wei said.
